subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Id-ul-Adha remembers the willingness of which prophet to sacrifice his son in obedience to God?
questions.explain: Id-ul-Adha commemorates Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to God.

options: Angels who serve and obey God
questions.explain: Malaikah are angels, beings created by God who carry out his commands, such as Jibril.

questions.q: On the Day of Judgement, Muslims believe people will be:
options: Judged by God on their deeds and sent to Paradise or Hell
questions.explain: Muslims believe God will judge each person by their actions, leading to Paradise or Hell.
Akhirah is the belief in life after death and an eternal existence beyond this life.

options: The first four leaders of the Muslim community after Muhammad
questions.explain: The rightly-guided caliphs were the first four leaders of the Muslim community after Muhammad.

questions.q: Belief in Tawhid means Muslims reject:
options: Associating any partners or equals with God (shirk)
questions.explain: Because God is one, Muslims reject shirk, the sin of associating partners with God.

questions.q: In Islam, Muhammad is regarded as:
options: The final prophet (the Seal of the Prophets)
questions.explain: Muslims believe Muhammad is the last and final prophet, the Seal of the Prophets.

questions.q: In Islam, the 'greater Jihad' refers to:
options: The personal struggle to be a good Muslim and resist temptation
questions.explain: The greater Jihad is the inner, personal struggle to live faithfully and overcome temptation.

questions.q: Zakah is the pillar of Islam that involves:
options: Giving a set portion of wealth to those in need
questions.explain: Zakah is giving a fixed share of one's wealth (usually 2.5%) to help those in need.

options: The outward struggle or military defence of Islam under strict conditions
questions.explain: The lesser Jihad is the outward struggle, including the defence of Islam under strict ethical conditions.

questions.q: The first Islamic community was established by Muhammad in:
questions.explain: After leaving Makkah, Muhammad established the first Muslim community in Madinah.

questions.q: The main cause of the Sunni-Shia split was disagreement over:
options: Who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad's death
questions.explain: The split arose over who should be the rightful leader of Muslims after Muhammad died.
